This experiment keeps 256 threads per block but maps them as 32x8, with contiguous x lanes in every warp, to test a practical row-tiled mapping against the flattened mapping. Direct loads avoid shared memory and barriers; the eight halo mappings exactly follow the baseline. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

model_interpretation.claim: The baseline is correct and averages 3.494 μs across three samples, but there is no profiling evidence isolating its bottleneck. items.subject: Coalesced direct-global stencil without shared memory
items.objective: Implement and measure a single-pass direct-global stencil with one output per thread and no shared memory or block-wide barriers. Map warp lanes to contiguous x elements; compare practical launch mappings and unroll the eight neighbor terms. Reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping for every offset, produce all 64³ outputs from current A on every call, and use no extra launch or allocation. Validate against the independent oracle and compare full-run event latency with the baseline.
